# v2026.11.02

This release hardens credential updates, translation diagnostics and private JSON persistence. It also adds a 95% Linux statement-coverage gate and reduces history decoding work.

## Fixes and boundaries

An authorized settings change could update a provider's Keychain item before the new settings file was committed. If that file commit failed, a subsequent request could send the new credential to the old endpoint. Concurrent reads could also combine an old configuration with a new credential. Exploitation requires a credential/endpoint update plus the relevant failure or race, and observation or control of the old endpoint; this is not an authentication bypass.

Credential mutations now follow a durable `pendingCredentialIDs` marker. Single and parallel translations stop while recovery is pending. Configuration and credentials are read as one process-local snapshot, with no settings lock held over upstream network calls. Recovery requires explicitly setting, clearing or removing each affected identity. Already-absent Keychain deletion is idempotent. New frontend cards retain their identity across retries; changing an identity or deleting the marker is not a recovery procedure.

Provider error bodies, malformed success bodies, arbitrary frontend event payloads and JSON decoder values no longer become diagnostics. Error kinds and HTTP status remain available; `APIError.Detail` stays source-compatible but is not populated or formatted. Known input-validation messages remain; unexpected errors use generic messages. Access logs use route patterns and bounded unmatched/method labels, and classify uncommitted HTTP errors without swallowing them. Existing logs and records are not rewritten.

History and settings now use a private same-directory temporary file, file synchronization, atomic replacement and directory synchronization. Pre-replacement failures preserve the committed file. A post-replacement directory-sync error explicitly reports that replacement committed; inspect current data before retrying an append. Symlink, non-regular and read-only targets are rejected. History initialization failure is reported and retried after storage recovery; clearing no longer reports success when removal or initialization fails.

The application dependency `golang.org/x/net` is updated to v0.62.0. Go 1.27.3 and Wails beta.28 are carried forward, not new upgrades in this release. Bun is pinned to the verified 1.4.4 build tool.

## Compatibility and recovery

Healthy existing settings, history keys and Keychain account names need no migration. `pendingCredentialIDs` is a new optional settings/status field; provider status adds `apiKeyNeedsConfirmation`. Valid request and successful translation shapes are unchanged; malformed request errors remain HTTP 400 with fixed messages.

Stop the old application and drain in-flight requests before replacement. Use one instance per configuration directory; no cross-process file lock or cross-store atomic transaction is claimed. Old binaries ignore pending markers, so do not run mixed versions. Complete explicit recovery and confirm the marker is empty and endpoint/credential correspondence is correct before rollback. Restoring only old JSON or deleting a marker can reintroduce a mismatched credential.

Recovery displays the last committed address, not an automatically restored failed edit. Confirm the intended endpoint before re-entering or clearing its key. Unfinished new providers appear as recovery cards that must be completed or explicitly removed. Repair storage/Keychain failures first, then save and verify the pending list is empty before resuming translation.

Preserve and protect the existing configuration directory. Convert intentional symlinks to private regular files before upgrade; atomic replacement changes the inode and does not preserve existing ACLs, extended attributes or hard-link copies. The filesystem must support file/directory synchronization and same-directory rename, with space for both versions. Persist the directory rather than individual JSON bind mounts. Process termination may leave private `.kakapo-*.tmp` files; stop all instances and inspect them before retention or cleanup. Clearing history does not remove these files, backups or exports.

Older history, logs, backups, exports and provider-side copies may contain sensitive content from previous error handling or a failed credential update. Restrict access, inspect and handle retained/exported copies under the applicable retention policy, and rotate credentials that may have been exposed. New code does not automatically rewrite existing copies or sanitize normal successful translations. These historical-data handling requirements are carry-forward operational duties, not evidence that this upgrade cleaned old data.

## Validation and performance

Linux amd64 and arm64, Go 1.27.3, real GTK/WebKit build dependencies and production frontend assets: 79 Go tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; 936/976 statements (95.90%), race detection, vet, build, formatting, license checks and actionlint passed. Bun: 2 provider-identity tests passed; their module has 100% function/line coverage, not whole-frontend coverage. Locked frontend installation, Wails binding generation and both frontend pages built on Linux. CI enforces the same coverage gate on the final source; the macOS workflow builds both amd64 and arm64 slices and verifies the universal bundle before publishing.

Real Linux filesystem tests cover write-size limits and SIGKILL before/after replacement. Credential recovery tests include synthetic memory/file-backed services, committed operations with lost acknowledgements, concurrent snapshots and a fresh process after SIGKILL. Separate native macOS integration passed 23 tests with race detection, 0 failed and 0 skipped, covering real file synchronization/replacement and synthetic credentials in an isolated real Keychain namespace. This does not verify locked user sessions, authorization prompts or GUI interaction. CI and release jobs require these native checks plus strict application-signature and universal-architecture verification. Bundles use the existing ad-hoc signing process; Developer ID signing and notarization are not provided. Bundle metadata remains the historical 0.1.0; the calendar release version, commit and build time are injected into the About metadata.

Eight interleaved Linux decode benchmark pairs, 50 entries and one Go CPU: median time changed from 5.996 ms to 3.271 ms with one result per entry, and 22.414 ms to 8.638 ms with six. Measured median throughput changed from 31.82 to 63.22 MB/s and 23.83 to 62.30 MB/s. Allocation bytes changed from 577,698 to 229,623 and 2,083,447 to 638,444; allocations from 1,010 to 409 and 3,311 to 1,059. A prior sequential batch was noisy and regressed in one scenario; these shared-host microbenchmarks are not end-to-end guarantees.

Durable history append has a cost: eight interleaved 50-iteration samples changed median time from 58.005 to 63.318 microseconds, bytes from 47,992 to 49,233 and allocations from 72 to 88. No blanket write-speed or overall application-latency improvement is claimed.
